I have created a schematic for my guitar pedal, a distortion pedal. It is a simple design with no bypass, meaning it is always on.  A5 is input and D29 is output. It has simple one pot design which is volume knob and currently you can't change the gain or tone on the pedal. It is currently a design i am working on for a bigger multi board project. This is based on this youtube video i Have watched by Tone Charm Audio, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RXIqUyW2syU

I finally got a working 9v splitter working for the guitar distortion pedal.  To get it work I took inspiration from some of the Boss pedal series where they split the input voltage (9v) into 4.5v as guitar sounds use ac while pedals use dc current. To fix this you halve the 9v into half to use the centre as the 0 of the ac current so it will be able to rise and fall within 9v without falling bellow 0v.

I used two 10K resistors in series with a capacitor in the middle to even out the flow which will result in near perfect at 4.5v. ( done in Tinkercad Circuit mode)

From my 9v splitter i had created a Boss DS1 replica .  From an average Boss pedal there are only  few tones to create from one pedal. Both individual pedals and multi boards cost a lot, to create more tones you had to buy a multi board or multiple  analog pedals which will add up and will take up space.  I saw multiple DIY guitar pedals using breadboards which cost a fraction of the cost. Instead of a generic DS1 this has 8 extra option which create new sounds from 80s to modern tones. Instead of a 4 way switch I used 3 slide switches to create 4 options and to create  these new sounds i used different resistance resistors at the gain clip off and between the amp gain stage and ground which controls how much sound is grounded. In theory these should work, done in Tinkercad Circuit mode. I t contains three different knobs gain, tone, and level all changed by the different resistor going into ground. (The piezo on the left is the input 1/4" jack and the right  is the output 1/4".

Tested the old schematic for the mod and discovered it didn't work most of the times because of some incorrect wiring which lead to a short. The new schematic was created on LIVESPICE so I can test it with my guitar. From the tests it is able to create harsh metal zone, slightly pushed, DS1, and a blues driver sound each with a unique sound. To use Live spice it will require a powerful CPU as it is CPU heavy

Drive to get Schematic for LIVESPICE: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/17vQvUrKN64YnFsDCXS0r1yeKk3elkCAl?usp=drive_link
To use press the green arrow or simulate
